newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA subject of federal probe - official.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA subject of federal probe - official.

text.p: The U.S. attorney's office confirmed Thursday that Columbia/HCA Healthcare, the world's largest for-profit hospital chain, was the target of a a federal investigation.
The probe follows the indictment of three executives on July 30 on charges of falsifying Medicare claims.

Sam Armstrong, spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Tampa, Fla., told Reuters that during an indictment hearing at Fort Myers, Fla., prosecutor Kathleen Haley had said the company itself was also under investigation.
Haley also said there may be a conflict of interest in the company's having the same lawyers as the indicted executives, Armstrong said.
"Other than that I can't comment," Armstrong said.
A U.S. magistrate Wednesday ordered that documents relating to the investigation into Colombia/Healthcare remain sealed, a court official said.
At a hearing in Tampa, Judge Tom McCoun denied a request from two newspapers, the Tampa Tribune and the St.Petersburg Times, to unseal FBI affidavits, she said.
Haley argued that it was too early to release the papers and the probe could be jeopardized. She said indictments involving more people could follow.

The three executives, Robert Whitesides, Jay Jarrell and Michael Neeb are due to be appear in court Tuesday in Fort Myers for arraignment on charges of fraud and conspiracy relating to alleged false claims at a Port Charlotte, Fla., hospital.
If convicted, they could face up to 25 years in prison and fines of $1.25 million.
